proposal: The Mandate recommends reducing federal subsidies for transit expansion: ending or, at a minimum, subjecting every Capital Investment Grants project to rigorous cost-benefit standards, ending use of the Highway Trust Fund to support mass transit, and returning the transit labor protection in the former Section 13(c) to its original intent so agencies can adjust fringe benefits. It also suggests redefining public transit as transit provided for the public, which would require legislation.
remaining: Enactment of a surface transportation reauthorization that ends or reduces Highway Trust Fund support for transit; the House committee bill increases Mass Transit Account authorizations instead, and transit authorizations run through 2026-12-11.

Finalization of the proposed 2026 CIG guidance, and any proposal to eliminate CIG, which the Mandate notes the first Trump administration sought (the FY2027 request cuts CIG to $1.2 billion from $1.7 billion but funds existing agreements and projects ready for construction, the House FY2027 appropriations bill provides about $737 million, and the 2026-07-22 letter does not mention CIG).
Any action to return the transit labor protections to their original scope; none was found, and H.R. 8870 does not change them according to CRS.
Legislation redefining public transit as transit provided for the public rather than by a public agency; none was identified.

status_summary: The administration has proposed part of these changes and Congress has enacted none. Secretary Duffy's letter of 2026-07-22 asks Congress to eliminate the Highway Trust Fund's Mass Transit Account, and FTA proposed Capital Investment Grants guidance on 2026-10-01 that would raise the cost-effectiveness weight to 25 percent and require 50 percent non-CIG funding before Engineering, after final guidance of 2025-11-12 left cost-effectiveness unchanged. DOT's FY2027 request (2026-04-03) cuts CIG to $1.2 billion from $1.7 billion without proposing to end it, and the House Appropriations Committee's FY2027 bill (H.R. 9170, reported 2026-06-05) provides about $737 million for CIG by transfer of unobligated rail funds. The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee's reauthorization bill (H.R. 8870, ordered reported 2026-05-22) would authorize $3.0 billion a year for CIG and keep trust fund support for transit, transit authorizations run through 2026-12-11 under H.R. 6500 (signed 2026-09-02), and no change to the Section 13(c) protections (now 49 U.S.C. 5333(b)) was found.

timeline.event: FTA publishes final Capital Investment Grants policy guidance (90 FR 50886), effective immediately. It replaces the vehicle-miles-traveled environmental benefits method with a pre-2013 approach based on EPA air quality designations, removes the social cost of carbon (citing EO 14154) and leaves the cost-effectiveness criterion unchanged.

DOL submits for OMB review a routine information collection for Protections for Transit Workers under Section 5333(b) (the former Section 13(c)); the notice shows the program continuing, and no action to narrow it was found.

DOT releases its FY2027 budget request. The Budget Highlights request $1.2 billion for Capital Investment Grants (down from $1.7 billion in FY2026 and $2.2 billion in FY2025), to fund existing New Starts agreements and projects that may be ready for construction, and $14.95 billion for Transit Formula Grants; they do not propose ending Capital Investment Grants (release date from DOT's budget page; the Highlights page was last updated 2026-05-05).

The House Transportation and Infrastructure chair introduces H.R. 8870, the BUILD America 250 Act (ordered reported 2026-05-22). Per CRS it authorizes about $17.5 billion a year in transit formula contract authority, $3.0 billion a year for CIG subject to appropriation, a voluntary consolidated state block grant for transit formula funds, and no change to Section 13(c).

House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee approves H.R. 8870 after a 14-hour markup, per the committee's release; GovInfo BILLSTATUS records the bill ordered reported as amended by a 62-2 vote, with no later House floor or Senate action (a Smart Cities Dive article gives 2026-05-17, which conflicts with the committee and CRS dates).

The House Appropriations Committee reports H.R. 9170, the FY2027 THUD appropriations bill (H. Rept. 119-686; full committee markup on 2026-06-03 per CRS). The reported text provides $737,193,000 for Capital Investment Grants, derived by transfer from unobligated infrastructure-law Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail balances, below the $1.7 billion enacted for FY2026 and the $1.215 billion request (CRS); the bill has had no House floor action.

Secretary Duffy writes to the chairs and ranking members of three Senate committees with the administration's reauthorization priorities, including eliminating the Highway Trust Fund's Mass Transit Account and moving all federal fuel tax revenue into the Highway Account, and conditioning transit formula funds on progress against crime and fare evasion, with up to 100 percent withholding. The letter (read in full from the copy posted by the American Road & Transportation Builders Association) does not mention Capital Investment Grants, Section 5333(b) labor protections or a definition of public transportation. The American Public Transportation Association says elimination would put more than 85 percent of federal transit and passenger rail funding at risk, per Smart Cities Dive.
timeline.source: Secretary of Transportation (copy posted by ARTBA)

timeline.event: The President signs H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027, which funds agencies through 2026-12-11 and extends authorities including surface transportation, per the White House statement. The enrolled text on GovInfo shows Division C is the Surface Transportation Extension Act of 2026 (Secs. 3001 to 3201), with appropriations and most extensions running to 2026-12-11 and Highway Trust Fund expenditure authority to 2026-12-12. CRS reports that the 2021 infrastructure law's transit authorizations were extended through 2026-12-11 under H.R. 6500 and that reauthorization is pending, with H.R. 8870 as the main vehicle.

FTA publishes proposed CIG policy guidance (comments due 2026-11-16) that would use one cost-per-linked-trip measure for cost-effectiveness with a 25 percent weight, raise required non-CIG funding commitments before Engineering from 30 to 50 percent for New Starts and Core Capacity, set the federal share starting at 40 percent, and add a safety and crime enrichment category.

title: Curb federal transit subsidies: tighten CIG, end Trust Fund transit support, narrow 13(c)
uncertainties: The Duffy letter was read in full from the copy hosted by ARTBA (not by DOT); it proposes eliminating the Mass Transit Account and does not mention CIG, Section 5333(b) or a definition of public transportation. The CRS report (read in part) says the letter did not identify a replacement funding source for most transit programs. Smart Cities Dive reports that H.R. 8870 would provide $87.6 billion from the Mass Transit Account for FY2027 to FY2031, up from $69.8 billion under the 2021 infrastructure law; the article date (approximately 2026-07-24) is inferred and the CRS figures differ in form and were not reconciled. The FY2027 request for CIG was read in DOT's Budget Highlights, not the full budget estimates; the administration's first-term proposal to eliminate CIG is mentioned only in the Mandate. GovInfo BILLSTATUS shows H.R. 8870 had no action after the 2026-05-22 committee vote (62-2), and the transit title of the introduced bill was not reached in the fetch, so its transit figures rest on CRS. The House FY2027 THUD bill's CIG amount and transfer source were read in the reported text and CRS; the bill does not state why the level is below the request, and BILLSTATUS gives no committee vote date (the 2026-06-03 markup date is from CRS). The DOL notices show only that the 5333(b) program continues. The CIG guidance does not implement the Mandate's rigorous cost-benefit ask until finalized, and the Mandate's secondary suggestion (redefining public transit) was not researched. Federal Register queries since 2026-10-02 showed no new FTA policy notice on CIG or Section 5333(b).
